prs.title: feat(home): play a chosen title on the TV
prs.body:
## What changed

`@home play Ithinno Aadame on jstv` used to open YouTube's home page while the assistant said it was playing. There was no tool that could take a title. The new `tv_play` tool takes a title and an app, and YouTube is the default.

With `/home lookups on`:

| App | Android TV | LG webOS | Home Assistant TVs |
|---|---|---|---|
| YouTube | Starts the top match | Starts the top match | Starts the top match if the TV accepts links |
| YouTube Music | Starts the top match | Starts the top match in YouTube | Starts the top match if the TV accepts links |
| Netflix, Prime Video, Disney+, Hotstar and other apps JustWatch lists | Opens the title's page | Opens the title's page | Opens the title's page if the TV accepts links |
| Spotify | Opens a search | Only opens the app | Opens a search if the TV accepts links |
| Any other app | Only opens the app | Only opens the app | Only opens the app |

With lookups off, which is the default, nothing is sent. YouTube, YouTube Music, Netflix, Prime Video, Disney+ and Spotify get a search where the TV takes links. Everything else only opens.

- The tool's answer says whether it sent a video, opened a page, ran a search or only opened the app. The assistant is told not to say something is playing otherwise.
- If a lookup fails or finds nothing, the app gets a search or is opened.
- A catalogue link is used only if the title matches what was asked for. An exact name beats a near one, and a subscription beats a rental.
- Only a value shaped like a video ID is taken from YouTube's page, only a plain `https://` link is taken from JustWatch, and titles are percent-encoded.
- On Home Assistant, the lookup runs only if the TV takes `play_media`. A refused link falls back to opening the app.

## Separate fix

Any `https://` request through ureq panicked, because `native-tls-no-default` doesn't turn on the feature ureq checks at runtime. This would have crashed on the first lookup. It also affects Home Assistant over `https://`. The fix has its own commit and adds `webpki-root-certs` to the build.

## Privacy

Lookups are off until someone runs `/home lookups on [COUNTRY]`. Once on, titles go from this machine to youtube.com or apis.justwatch.com, including `@home play X` with no app named. The country comes from the language setting unless one is given. The README says all of this.

## Known limitations

- A title page is one press short of playing. Nothing presses play for you.
- Spotify stays a search, because its IDs take an account to look up.
- The top YouTube result can be the wrong video.
- Both lookups use unofficial interfaces, so a change on their side breaks them. A YouTube results page with no videos on it is reported to the owner.
- The search links are unverified, and an app may ignore them or a title link.

## Testing

- `cargo test` passes and clippy reports no warnings. CI passes on `ffc0d23`.
- Live lookups through the real HTTP client returned a YouTube video ID and a Netflix title link.
- Home Assistant `play` is tested against the fake hub, including no `play_media` and a refused link.
- The webOS launch payloads are unit tested. The Netflix webOS payload format has not been confirmed against any source or device.
- The Android TV and webOS `play` paths have no end-to-end tests.
- Not tried on any real TV.
